content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"CORE_ONLY","rationale":"The supplied texts most directly identify righteousness with conduct commanded by God. Deuteronomy 6:25 calls observing the commandments “our righteousness”; Psalm 119:172 says the commandments are righteousness; and 1 John 3:7 expressly links being righteous with doing righteousness. Revelation 19:8 further identifies the wedding linen as the saints’ righteous acts, strongly supporting the chapter’s conduct-and-garment connection. The strongest counter-reading rightly observes that these passages do not establish an exhaustive definition for every biblical use of righteousness, particularly Pauline justification language. That objection limits the book’s universalizing claims but does not furnish a better explanation of the evidence actually concentrated here. The core claim that righteousness in this scriptural pattern is commanded conduct is therefore persuasive, while many broader symbolic and lexical elaborations remain unproved.","book_core_identification":"Righteousness is the doing of what God commands—obedient, righteous conduct—rather than merely a forensic status or an undefined quality of goodness.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The garment symbol uniformly represents the covenant worn through righteous acts.","The wedding guest lacked righteous acts and was condemned specifically for that absence.","God gives or enables the righteous deeds, while the believer must actively put them on and continue in them.","Covenant covering and the garment of conduct form a fixed sequence: entry into covenant followed by covenant obedience.","Dirty garments represent righteous deeds stained by the doer’s sins and subsequently cleansed by Christ’s blood.","Foot washing symbolizes repeated cleansing of one’s daily conduct after the one-time covenantal washing of baptism.","Fig leaves symbolize self-defined righteousness, whereas divinely supplied clothing represents obedience according to God’s pattern.","Every component of the armor of God belongs to a unified symbolic wardrobe ultimately identified with putting on Christ.","The garment terminology throughout Scripture consistently distinguishes covenant faithfulness from covenant-breaking nakedness."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"Righteousness is the broader condition of rightness according to God’s standard, encompassing ethical obedience in the cited passages but also God-given covenantal or forensic standing in other contexts.
